newsitem.title: UK: British Labour's Cook to set out European plan.
newsitem.headline: British Labour's Cook to set out European plan.

text.p: The opposition Labour party is to pledge on Tuesday to take Britain to the heart of Europe, but without discarding "hard-headed economics" when it has to decide on whether or not to join a European single currnecy.
The pledges are expected in a speech to 100 businessmen in London by Labour's foreign affairs spokesman Robin Cook, who is hitting the campaign trail for the May 1 election.

Aides said Cook, who has gradually softened his sceptical stance on Europe, will argue that Labour will replace the isolation Britain is suffering in Europe due to Conservative policies with strategic alliances.

Cook is also due to unveil a six-point "business plan" for Europe, which includes Labour's pledge to complete the single market and to decide on the single currency "on the basis of hard-headed economics not political dogma".

He is also expected to attack the Conservatives for failing to protect Britain's interests in Europe, taking as an example the government's inability to end the export ban on British beef imposed by Europe because of fears of mad cow disease.

Labour has argued that the Conservatives, deeply split on Europe and trailing in the opinion polls, mishandled the announcement of scientific findings showing there might be a danger of catching the human equivalent of mad cow disease, prompting consumer panic.

Cook, the officials said, "will stress that the real Euro-danger is the increasing hostility of the Tory (Conservative) party to Europe, which is sweeping Britain towards the exit door from Europe". -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
